declaredDifferences: .angular-cli.json apps[0].environments.dev names the same file as environmentSource, which is the identity swap the era CLI performed for its default environment; it needs no fileReplacements and was synthesized as the target's unconfigured default rather than as a named configuration

the era `ng build --prod` flag set ahead-of-time compilation, the build optimiser, full output hashing and CSS extraction and turned off source maps, named chunks and the vendor chunk. Those flags were written into the production configuration, because on a 16.2 line they are configuration rather than command-line flags. CSS extraction is unconditional there and has no option left, so it is not restated

.angular-cli.json was replaced by angular.json: the Angular CLI 1.x workspace format is not read by any 16.2 toolchain, so leaving it in the tree would leave a file that describes the build and is never consulted

projects.tiny-translator.architect.lint ran @angular-devkit/build-angular:tslint, and angular-16-browser-builder carries no TSLint line. The target was removed as a declared migration difference: the era workspace lints with TSLint and the migrated workspace does not, and no replacement lint capability was chosen here.

tslint.json configures TSLint, and angular-16-browser-builder carries no TSLint line for it to configure. The file was removed with the targets that read it; no rule in it was translated to another linter.

dependencies.@angular/http was removed: the migrated workspace no longer carries it. @angular/http stops at 7.2.16 and is deprecated on the registry with "Package no longer supported. Use @angular/common instead". Angular removed the package after the 7 line; there is no 8.x and no 16.x, so the `@angular/` family range this cell writes for its own packages names a version that was never published. The HTTP client that succeeded it is `@angular/common/http`, an entry point of a package this cell already carries, so the dependency is dropped rather than pinned to a v7 line beside a v16 framework.

devDependencies.codelyzer was removed: the migrated workspace no longer carries it. codelyzer stops at 6.0.2, a TSLint rule set for Angular 9-era workspaces. Nothing succeeds it on the TSLint line and its ESLint replacement is @angular-eslint, which this cell already aligns as a family.

devDependencies.tslint was removed: the migrated workspace no longer carries it. TSLint stops at 6.1.3 and was deprecated by its own maintainers in favour of ESLint before Angular 13 shipped. There is no TSLint release for any Angular line at or beyond this cell, so the whole TSLint toolchain is dropped rather than carried.
unhandled: projects.tiny-translator.architect.e2e used @angular-devkit/build-angular:protractor, which the 16.2 devkit does not ship; the target was removed and no replacement capability was chosen for it
devDependencies.karma-cli is coupled to the Angular test cell but is not part of the toolchain angular-16-browser-builder generates, so it was left at its era range
devDependencies.karma-coverage-istanbul-reporter is coupled to the Angular test cell but is not part of the toolchain angular-16-browser-builder generates, so it was left at its era range
compilerOptions.lib was left as declared; the 16.2 line does not require a specific lib set and narrowing one could remove a type surface the application relies on

src/app/rxjs-operators.ts imports rxjs/add/observable/combineLatest, an RxJS 5 patch module that RxJS 6 removed along with the prototype patching it performed. Removing the import alone would leave the operator call sites it enabled calling a method that no longer exists, so it is reported rather than rewritten: the call sites have to move to `pipe` first.
